# One live run of a quiz (a rehearsal, the real talk, ...) with its own players
# and answers. Players join from their phones at /play/<code>.
#
# The moderator moves the game on, one step at a time (see #take_step):
#
#   lobby --start--> open --finish--> closed --next--> open ... --end--> ended
#
# Each shown question is a Round. Games skip inactive questions: the next
# question is always the first active question of the quiz (in quiz order) that
# this game has not shown yet, so switching a question off, or on, during a
# game is taken into account at the next step.
#
# After the end, the big screen shows the leaderboard (Game::Leaderboard) and
# the moderator picks the winners (#pick_winners).
#
# +version+ grows with every step and every change of the winners. Screens and
# phones use it to tell a newer state from an older one, and the moderator's
# step buttons send the version they were shown with, so a double click or a
# stale second screen cannot skip a question.
class Game < ApplicationRecord
  CODE_ALPHABET = "ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789".chars.freeze # no 0/O, 1/I/L
  CODE_LENGTH = 5
  STEPS = %w[ start finish next end ].freeze
  WINNER_PICKS = %w[ top draw reset ].freeze

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :rounds, -> { order(:number) }, dependent: :delete_all, inverse_of: :game
  has_many :players, dependent: :delete_all, inverse_of: :game

  enum :status, %w[ lobby playing ended ].index_by(&:itself), default: "lobby", validate: true

  before_validation :assign_code, on: :create
  validates :code, presence: true

  scope :newest_first, -> { order(created_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  # Codes are shown in capitals; people may type them in lower case.
  def self.find_by_code(code)
    find_by(code: code.to_s.strip.upcase)
  end

  # The round shown last (the current one while the game is playing).
  def current_round
    rounds.reorder(number: :desc).first
  end

  # :lobby, :open (players can answer), :closed (results shown) or :ended.
  def phase
    if ended? then :ended
    elsif lobby? then :lobby
    elsif current_round&.open? then :open
    else :closed
    end
  end

  # Active questions this game has not shown yet, in quiz order.
  def questions_left
    quiz.questions.active.where.not(id: rounds.select(:question_id))
  end

  def last_question?
    !questions_left.exists?
  end

  # Shown questions plus the ones still to come ("Question 2 of 5").
  def questions_total
    rounds.count + questions_left.count
  end

  def leaderboard
    Game::Leaderboard.new(self)
  end

  # Applies a moderator's step ("start", "finish", "next" or "end") if the game
  # is still at +seen_version+ and the step fits the current phase. Returns
  # true when the game moved on (it is then broadcast to phones and screens).
  def take_step(step, seen_version:)
    return false unless step.in?(STEPS)

    moved = transaction do
      reload
      next false unless version == seen_version.to_i && send(:"#{step}_step")

      self.version += 1
      save!
    end

    broadcast_change if moved
    moved
  end

  # The prizes, once the game is over: "top" ("Top N"), "draw" ("Draw") or
  # "reset" ("Reset winners"), N being the quiz's number of winners. Every
  # draw draws again. Returns true when the winners changed (they are then
  # broadcast to phones and screens).
  #
  # Unlike steps, these need no version: they always apply to the current
  # leaderboard, and repeating one is harmless (Turbo also disables a button
  # while its click is being sent).
  def pick_winners(how)
    return false unless how.in?(WINNER_PICKS)

    changed = transaction do
      reload
      next false unless ended?

      winner_ids =
        case how
        when "top" then leaderboard.top(quiz.winners_count)
        when "draw" then leaderboard.draw(quiz.winners_count)
        else []
        end.map(&:player_id).sort
      next false if winner_ids == players.where(winner: true).order(:id).ids

      now = Time.current
      players.where(winner: true).where.not(id: winner_ids).update_all(winner: false, updated_at: now)
      players.where(id: winner_ids, winner: false).update_all(winner: true, updated_at: now)
      self.version += 1
      save!
    end

    broadcast_change if changed
    changed
  end

  # Pushes the change to the phones (PlayChannel: their new stage) and the big
  # screens (ScreenChannel: the new version, they reload), right away, so that
  # every phone gets a new question at the same moment.
  def broadcast_change
    PlayChannel.broadcast_stage(self)
    ScreenChannel.broadcast_version(self)
  rescue StandardError => error
    # The change is saved; phones and screens catch up on their next sync or poll.
    Rails.error.report(error, handled: true)
  end

  private
    def assign_code
      self.code ||= loop do
        candidate = Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET.sample(random: SecureRandom) }.join
        break candidate unless Game.exists?(code: candidate)
      end
    end

    def start_step
      lobby? && open_next_round
    end

    def finish_step
      return false unless phase == :open

      current_round.close
      true
    end

    # "Next", or the end of the game when no active question is left.
    def next_step
      return false unless phase == :closed

      open_next_round || end_step
    end

    def end_step
      return false if ended?

      current_round&.close
      self.status = "ended"
      self.ended_at = Time.current
      true
    end

    def open_next_round
      question = questions_left.first
      return false unless question

      rounds.create!(question: question, number: rounds.maximum(:number).to_i + 1, opened_at: Time.current)
      self.status = "playing"
      self.started_at ||= Time.current
      true
    end
end
EOF

# What a player's phone shows: the lobby, the open question, the results of
# the closed question, or the end (the player's place and points, and whether
# they won). The play page, PlayChannel (pushes), the polling endpoint and the
# answer endpoint all render it (play/_stage), from the database's state.
#
# Nothing about the correct options is exposed while a round is open: they
# are only read once the round is closed (#revealed?). Points are only shown
# at the end.
#
# A stage is first built for the whole game, then personalized for a player
# (#for_player): the player's pick in the round, or their standing at the end.
# Broadcasts render one variant per possible pick (#variants), not one page per
# player; at the end, they carry every player's standing (#standings) and each
# subscription renders its own (see PlayChannel).
class Game::Stage
  # A player's result at the end: "Place 2 of 5", "3 points", "You won!".
  Standing = Data.define(:place, :players_count, :points, :winner) do
    alias_method :winner?, :winner

    # The player's standing out of #standings (as broadcast), or nil.
    def self.from_standings(standings, player_id)
      place, points, winner = standings&.dig("places", player_id.to_s)
      new(place: place, players_count: standings["players"], points: points, winner: winner == 1) if place
    end
  end

  attr_reader :game, :version, :phase, :round, :question, :options, :position, :total,
    :answer_option_id, :revision, :standing

  # The player's pick in a round. +key+ identifies it among the #variants.
  def self.answer_part(player, round_id)
    option_id, revision = Answer.where(round_id: round_id, player_id: player.id).pick(:option_id, :revision)
    { key: option_id.to_s, answer_option_id: option_id, revision: revision || 0 }
  end

  # +version+ and +phase+ can be given to build the end of a game from a
  # broadcast, without reading the database.
  def initialize(game, version: game.version, phase: game.phase)
    @game = game
    @version = version
    @phase = phase
    if phase.in?(%i[ open closed ])
      @round = game.current_round
      @question = round&.question
      @options = question ? question.options.to_a : []
      @position = round&.position
      @total = game.questions_total
    end
    @options ||= []
    @revision = 0
  end

  # :answer (open and closed rounds), :standing (ended games) or nil (the lobby).
  def personal_kind
    if round then :answer
    elsif phase == :ended then :standing
    end
  end

  def for_player(player)
    case personal_kind
    when :answer
      personalized(**self.class.answer_part(player, round.id).except(:key))
    when :standing
      board = game.leaderboard
      entry = board.entry_for(player)
      with_standing(entry && Standing.new(place: entry.place, players_count: board.size, points: entry.points, winner: entry.winner?))
    else
      self
    end
  end

  def with_standing(standing)
    dup.tap { |stage| stage.instance_variable_set(:@standing, standing) }
  end

  # Every player's standing at the end, compact enough to broadcast to every
  # phone: { "players" => 5, "places" => { "<player id>" => [ place, points, 1 if winner else 0 ] } }.
  def standings
    board = game.leaderboard
    { "players" => board.size, "places" => board.entries.to_h { |entry| [ entry.player_id.to_s, [ entry.place, entry.points, entry.winner? ? 1 : 0 ] ] } }
  end

  # Every personalized stage a player can get during the game, keyed like
  # #answer_part. (In an open round there are no answers yet when it is
  # broadcast.) Not used at the end: see #standings.
  def variants
    case personal_kind
    when :answer
      [ nil, *(options.map(&:id) if revealed?) ].to_h { |option_id| [ option_id.to_s, personalized(answer_option_id: option_id) ] }
    else
      { "" => self }
    end
  end

  def question?
    question.present?
  end

  def revealed?
    phase == :closed && question?
  end

  def picked?(option)
    option.id == answer_option_id
  end

  # Only for a closed round.
  def correct?(option)
    revealed? && option.correct?
  end

  # :right, :wrong or :none once the round is closed.
  def result
    return unless revealed?
    return :none unless answer_option_id

    options.any? { |option| picked?(option) && option.correct? } ? :right : :wrong
  end

  def payload(html)
    { version: version, revision: revision, html: html }
  end

  private
    def personalized(answer_option_id: nil, revision: 0)
      dup.tap do |stage|
        stage.instance_variable_set(:@answer_option_id, answer_option_id)
        stage.instance_variable_set(:@revision, revision)
      end
    end
end
EOF

# Live updates for a player's phone (play_controller.js).
#
# - Every change of the game is broadcast once (Game#broadcast_change). During
#   the game, the message has the stage rendered for each possible personal
#   part (Game::Stage#variants); each subscription picks the player's variant
#   (one small query) and transmits it. At the end, the message has every
#   player's standing instead (Game::Stage#standings: place, points, winner),
#   and each subscription renders the player's own end stage, without queries.
# - The phone calls #sync right after subscribing (the confirmation comes once
#   the stream is set up, so nothing is missed in between), and then every few
#   seconds. It sends the version and revision it shows; if the server has
#   something newer, it is transmitted. Syncing also keeps the player present
#   (Presence), so a phone that silently dropped off stops counting.
#
# Messages to the phone: { version, revision, html }, or { gone: true } when
# the game or the player no longer exists.
class PlayChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  def self.broadcast_stage(game)
    stage = Game::Stage.new(game)
    message = { version: game.version, kind: stage.personal_kind }

    if stage.personal_kind == :standing
      message[:standings] = stage.standings
    else
      message[:round_id] = stage.round&.id
      message[:variants] = stage.variants.transform_values { |variant| render_stage(variant) }
    end

    broadcast_to(game, message)
  end

  def self.render_stage(stage)
    ApplicationController.render(partial: "play/stage", locals: { stage: stage })
  end

  def subscribed
    @game = Game.find_by_code(params[:code])
    @player = @game.players.find_by(browser_token: browser_token) if @game && browser_token
    return reject unless @player

    @presence_key = "cable:#{SecureRandom.uuid}"
    Presence.leave(@game.id, Presence.poll_key(@player.id)) # the cable takes over from HTTP
    touch_presence

    stream_for @game, coder: ActiveSupport::JSON do |message|
      deliver(message)
    end
  end

  def unsubscribed
    Presence.leave(@game.id, @presence_key) if @presence_key
  end

  def sync(data)
    touch_presence
    transmit_stage(unless_showing: [ data["version"], data["revision"] ])
  end

  private
    def touch_presence
      Presence.touch(@game.id, @player.id, @presence_key, ttl: Presence::CABLE_TTL)
    end

    # Transmits the player's current stage, unless the phone already shows it.
    def transmit_stage(unless_showing: nil)
      game = Game.find_by(id: @game.id)
      player = game&.players&.find_by(id: @player.id)
      return transmit({ gone: true }) unless player
      return if unless_showing && showing?(game, player, *unless_showing)

      stage = Game::Stage.new(game).for_player(player)
      transmit stage.payload(self.class.render_stage(stage))
    end

    # Whether the phone shows the current version and revision (checked
    # cheaply: most syncs find nothing new).
    def showing?(game, player, version, revision)
      return false unless version.is_a?(Integer) && revision.is_a?(Integer) && version == game.version

      round = game.current_round if game.playing?
      revision == (round ? round.answers.where(player: player).pick(:revision).to_i : 0)
    end

    def deliver(message)
      if message["kind"] == "standing"
        deliver_standing(message)
      else
        deliver_variant(message)
      end
    end

    def deliver_variant(message)
      personal = message["kind"] == "answer" ? Game::Stage.answer_part(@player, message["round_id"]) : { key: "" }
      html = message["variants"][personal[:key]]

      if html
        transmit({ version: message["version"], revision: personal[:revision] || 0, html: html })
      else
        transmit_stage # not one of the variants (say, an answer given before the broadcast arrived)
      end
    end

    def deliver_standing(message)
      standing = Game::Stage::Standing.from_standings(message["standings"], @player.id)
      return transmit_stage unless standing

      stage = Game::Stage.new(@game, version: message["version"], phase: :ended).with_standing(standing)
      transmit stage.payload(self.class.render_stage(stage))
    end
end
EOF
cat > app/channels/screen_channel.rb <<'EOF'
# Live updates for the big screens of a game (screen_controller.js): every
# change of the game (steps, winners) is pushed as { version } right away, and
# the screen reloads itself (a Turbo morph). So a big screen that is not the
# one the moderator clicks on (a projector, a second laptop) follows at once,
# not at its next poll.
#
# The big screen is moderator-only (HTTP Basic), which the WebSocket does not
# carry: the page subscribes with the game's signed id (#token_for), which only
# moderator pages contain.
class ScreenChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  PURPOSE = :big_screen

  def self.token_for(game)
    game.signed_id(purpose: PURPOSE)
  end

  def self.broadcast_version(game)
    broadcast_to(game, { version: game.version })
  end

  def subscribed
    game = Game.find_signed(params[:token].to_s, purpose: PURPOSE)
    return reject unless game

    stream_for game
  end
end
EOF

module GamesHelper
  QR_QUIET_ZONE = 3 # modules of white around the code; the .qr card adds about one more

  # The join link as an inline SVG QR code.
  def qr_code_svg(url, label:)
    qr = RQRCode::QRCode.new(url, level: :m)
    path = qr.as_svg(module_size: 1, use_path: true, standalone: false, color: "0d0640")
    size = qr.qrcode.module_count + 2 * QR_QUIET_ZONE

    tag.svg(path.html_safe, xmlns: "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", viewBox: "-#{QR_QUIET_ZONE} -#{QR_QUIET_ZONE} #{size} #{size}",
      "shape-rendering": "crispEdges", role: "img", aria: { label: label })
  end

  # A moderator's step on the big screen ("Start", "Finish", "Next", "End quiz").
  def game_step_button(game, label, step)
    button_to label, moderate_game_step_path(game), params: { step: step, version: game.version },
      class: "btn btn--pink btn--lg"
  end

  # The prize buttons after the end: "Top N" and "Draw" (+pick+ "top" or "draw").
  def game_winners_button(game, label, pick, style: "btn--pink")
    button_to label, moderate_game_winners_path(game), params: { pick: pick }, class: "btn #{style} btn--lg"
  end

  def reset_winners_button(game)
    button_to "Reset winners", moderate_game_winners_path(game), method: :delete, class: "btn btn--ghost btn--lg"
  end

  # Tooltip on a leaderboard score: the total time of the correct answers,
  # which ranks players with equal points.
  def leader_time(entry)
    "In #{number_with_precision(entry.time_us / 1_000_000.0, precision: 2)} s"
  end

  def game_status_label(game)
    case game.phase
    when :lobby then "Waiting for players"
    when :ended then "Over"
    else "Live"
    end
  end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class Game::LeaderboardTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Quiz", winners_count: 2)
    @first = create_question(@quiz, "First?", { "Right" => true, "Also right" => true, "Wrong" => false })
    @second = create_question(@quiz, "Second?", { "Yes" => true, "No" => false })
    @game = @quiz.games.create!
    @alice, @bob, @carol, @dave, @eve = %w[ Alice Bob Carol Dave Eve ].map { |name| @game.players.create!(name: name, browser_token: name) }
  end

  def step(name)
    @game.take_step(name, seen_version: @game.version)
  end

  # Opens a question, lets each player pick an option the given seconds after
  # the opening, and closes it.
  def play(question, picks)
    travel_to Time.zone.local(2026, 10, 8, 10, 0, 0) do
      @game.lobby? ? step("start") : step("next")
      round = @game.current_round
      assert_equal question, round.question

      picks.sort_by { |(_player, _option, seconds)| seconds }.each do |player, option, seconds|
        travel_to round.opened_at + seconds
        round.record_answer(player, question.options.find_by!(text: option).id)
      end
      step("finish")
    end
  end

  def board
    @game.leaderboard
  end

  def names(entries)
    entries.map(&:name)
  end

  test "ranks by points, then by the total time of the correct answers, then by joining" do
    play @first, [ [ @alice, "Right", 9 ], [ @bob, "Also right", 2 ], [ @carol, "Wrong", 1 ], [ @dave, "Right", 3 ] ]
    play @second, [ [ @alice, "Yes", 1 ], [ @bob, "No", 1 ], [ @carol, "Yes", 4 ] ]
    step("end")

    assert_equal %w[ Alice Bob Dave Carol Eve ], names(board.entries)
    assert_equal [ 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 ], board.entries.map(&:place)
    assert_equal [ 2, 1, 1, 1, 0 ], board.entries.map(&:points)
    assert_equal [ 10, 2, 3, 4, 0 ].map { |seconds| seconds * 1_000_000 }, board.entries.map(&:time_us),
      "only correct answers count, wrong ones add no time"
    assert_equal 5, board.size
  end

  test "an answer's time runs to the player's last pick" do
    travel_to Time.zone.local(2026, 10, 8, 10, 0, 0) do
      step("start")
      round = @game.current_round
      right, also_right, wrong = @first.options

      travel 1.second
      round.record_answer(@alice, wrong.id)
      round.record_answer(@bob, right.id)
      travel 2.seconds
      round.record_answer(@alice, right.id) # changed: the time is now 3 s
      round.record_answer(@bob, right.id)   # the same pick again: still 1 s
      travel 1.second
      round.record_answer(@carol, wrong.id)
      round.record_answer(@carol, also_right.id)

      assert_equal({ "Alice" => 3_000_000, "Bob" => 1_000_000, "Carol" => 4_000_000 },
        round.answers.includes(:player).to_h { |answer| [ answer.player.name, answer.elapsed_us ] })
    end
  end

  test "Top N takes the first N players, never those with 0 points" do
    play @first, [ [ @alice, "Right", 1 ], [ @bob, "Right", 2 ], [ @carol, "Right", 3 ] ]
    play @second, [ [ @carol, "Yes", 1 ] ]

    assert_equal %w[ Carol Alice ], names(board.top(2))
    assert_equal %w[ Carol Alice Bob ], names(board.top(10)), "fewer than N players with points: all of them"
    assert_equal %w[ Carol ], names(board.top(1))
  end

  test "Draw: everyone above the N-th place's points wins, the rest is drawn among the tied" do
    @quiz.update!(winners_count: 3)
    play @first, [ [ @alice, "Right", 1 ], [ @bob, "Right", 2 ], [ @carol, "Right", 3 ], [ @dave, "Right", 4 ] ]
    play @second, [ [ @dave, "Yes", 1 ] ]
    # Dave 2 points; Alice, Bob, Carol 1 point (in that order by speed); Eve 0.

    assert_equal %w[ Dave Alice Bob ], names(board.top(3))
    assert_equal %w[ Alice Bob Carol ], names(board.draw_pool(3))

    draws = 60.times.map { board.draw(3) }
    assert draws.all? { |winners| winners.size == 3 && winners.first.name == "Dave" }
    assert_equal %w[ Alice Bob Carol ], draws.flat_map { |winners| names(winners.drop(1)) }.uniq.sort, "speed does not matter in a draw"
    assert draws.all? { |winners| winners.none? { |entry| entry.name == "Eve" } }

    assert_equal names(board.draw(3, random: Random.new(1))), names(board.draw(3, random: Random.new(1)))
  end

  test "Draw without a tie on the N-th place, and with fewer players with points than prizes" do
    play @first, [ [ @alice, "Right", 1 ], [ @bob, "Right", 2 ] ]
    play @second, [ [ @alice, "Yes", 1 ] ]

    assert_empty board.draw_pool(2)
    assert_equal %w[ Alice Bob ], names(board.draw(2))
    assert_equal %w[ Alice ], names(board.draw(1))
    assert_equal %w[ Alice Bob ], names(board.draw(4))
  end

  test "a tie entirely inside the first N is not a draw" do
    play @first, [ [ @alice, "Right", 1 ], [ @bob, "Right", 2 ], [ @carol, "Wrong", 3 ] ]
    play @second, [ [ @carol, "Yes", 1 ] ]
    # Alice, Bob and Carol have 1 point each.

    assert_equal %w[ Alice Bob Carol ], names(board.draw_pool(2))
    assert_empty board.draw_pool(3)
    assert_equal %w[ Alice Bob Carol ], names(board.draw(3)).sort
  end

  test "without players" do
    @game.players.delete_all
    step("start")
    step("end")

    assert board.empty?
    assert_empty board.top(3)
    assert_empty board.draw(3)
  end
end
EOF

steps.message:
Prizes are in: the leaderboard, phone results, Top N / Draw / Reset winners, the "Number of winners" setting, and faster live updates. All 132 tests pass, RuboCop and Brakeman are clean, and no new gems were needed. I also ran it under `bin/serve` in production, both on an empty `storage/` and on the existing database, which migrates and keeps its quizzes.

**Results under `bin/serve`, in real browsers (a big screen, a second screen, four phones):**
- **Speed:** phones show each step 50–210 ms after the moderator's click, all within a few ms of each other. A second big screen follows in about 0.1–0.3 s; before, it only polled once a second.
- **Load:** with 300 simulated phones, every step reached all of them within 0.16 s. With 1000, a question took 0.34 s and the end screen 0.6–0.7 s.
- **Prizes:** the leaderboard order, each phone's "Place X of Y" and points, and "You won!" after Top N / Draw / Reset winners were all correct and updated live.
- **Without WebSockets:** phones and screens still follow by polling, a little slower (up to 3 s on phones).

**How it works:**
- **Timing:** answer times are measured on the server, from the moment the question opens to the player's last pick. Tapping the same option again doesn't change the time.
- **Ranking:**
  - more points first, then the lower total time of correct answers;
  - players still tied (in practice only those with 0 points) are ordered by who joined first, so places are always 1, 2, 3…;
  - places are recalculated each time, so later edits to a question's correct options change them.
- **Live updates:** they now go straight from the app process to the phones; the database relay waited up to 0.1 s per step. Big screens get a push on every change and re-render. This relies on the app running as one process, which it already did.
- **Labels:** all labels are exactly as specified. "Top N" and "Draw" are always shown after the end; "Reset winners" appears only while there are winners. That way nothing on the screen contains the word "winner" until someone wins, so a text search for "Winner" can't also hit that button. There are no confirmation dialogs on these buttons.

**Choices you may want to revisit:**
- The quiz export / import JSON is unchanged, so "Number of winners" isn't exported and imported quizzes get 3.
- "Number of winners" is capped at 10,000.
- On the big screen, hovering a player's points shows their total time (a tooltip only, no extra visible text).
- Under a heavy burst of answers, later picks also count the time spent queued on the server. Their order is kept, so the ranking isn't affected.

**A problem I hit and fixed:** on SQLite, changing or removing a column the Rails way rebuilds the table. That deleted every answer through the cascading foreign keys, in both the upgrade and the rollback (only on databases with data). The migration now only adds columns and uses SQLite's own column drop to roll back. Both directions are tested on real data and nothing is lost.

`docs/architecture.md` has the details, including the measured timings and this migration pitfall. `script/load_test.rb` now also measures the end screen and "Top 3".
